CVE-2026-117549.title: @fastify/secure-session vulnerable to signature verification bypass via cookie signature removal
CVE-2026-117549.description: @fastify/secure-session is a session plugin for Fastify that stores an encrypted session in a cookie. In versions 7.5.0 through 8.4.1, when the plugin is configured with the signed cookie option, it calls the cookie unsign routine but, when the signature check reports the value as invalid, still passes the original cookie value to the session decoder, so a session whose signature did not validate is decrypted anyway. The practical effect appears when an application supplies the cookie signing secret independently of the session encryption key and rotates only the signing secret to retire existing sessions while keeping the encryption key active, because a holder of an old session cookie can strip the now obsolete signature and keep using the session. The attacker must already possess an unexpired encrypted session cookie and needs neither secret, and cannot forge session data, extend expiry, or survive rotation of the encryption key. The issue is fixed in @fastify/secure-session…

CVE-2026-99407.title: xfs: don't repair fs summary counters with garbage
CVE-2026-99407.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: don't repair fs summary counters with garbage

LOLLM noticed that if we scan the filesystem and come up with totally
garbage numbers for the summary counters, we don't actually mark the
scan incomplete. Because we don't do this, repair can install the
garbage values into the filesystem, making things worse. Don't do that.

CVE-2026-99472.title: KVM: pfncache: use a dedicated invalidation sequence for cache refresh
CVE-2026-99472.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: pfncache: use a dedicated invalidation sequence for cache refresh

The gfn_to_pfn_cache refresh path guards against mmu notifier
invalidations which complete while it has dropped gpc->lock for the
HVA->PFN lookup: hva_to_pfn_retry() samples kvm->mmu_invalidate_seq
and retries if it changed, or if mn_active_invalidate_count is still
elevated.

That is insufficient for HVA-based caches. mmu_invalidate_seq is only
advanced by kvm_mmu_invalidate_end() when the invalidated range
overlaps a memslot, and an HVA-based cache (e.g. the Xen shared_info
page mapped with KVM_XEN_ATTR_TYPE_SHARED_INFO_HVA) need not be backed
by any memslot at all. An invalidation of the cached HVA which starts
and ends entirely within the lookup window is thus invisible to the
retry check: mn_active_invalidate_count is back to zero and the
sequence never moved. The refresh then publishes a mapping of a page
which has already been freed, and…

CVE-2026-99498.title: s390/kprobes: Prevent kprobes on instructions with exception table entry
CVE-2026-99498.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

s390/kprobes: Prevent kprobes on instructions with exception table entry

The mvcos exception handler ex_handler_ua_mvcos() decodes the faulting
instruction, assuming it is an mvcos instruction. In case the instruction
is kprobed the decoded instruction is a breakpoint instruction instead,
which leads to incorrect instruction decoding and potential register
corruption.

Fix this by simply preventing to set a kprobe on such instructions,
similar like arm64 is doing it.

CVE-2026-99616.title: ovl: look up the index by the decoded origin
CVE-2026-99616.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ovl: look up the index by the decoded origin

A file opened by file handle on an overlay with nfs_export=on can show
the stale lower data of a file that was copied up to the upper layer.
While the file opened this way stays in the inode cache, a lookup of the
copied up file by path fails with ESTALE for all users. The open can
also succeed for a file that was removed, where it has to fail with
ESTALE. This happens with a handle that has one byte changed. The handle
comes from an NFS client, or from a process that calls
open_by_handle_at() with CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH in the initial user
namespace.

When a file in a lower layer is about to be modified, overlayfs first
copies it to the upper layer (copy up). With nfs_export=on, each copy up
also creates an entry in the index directory, a directory that overlayfs
keeps for itself on the upper filesystem.
